one_liner: Senior Army cyber program analyst in Columbia, MD who leads technical experts in managing acquisition, cost, schedule, and performance for cyberspace capability programs.
fit_summary: This GG-13 role needs a year leading complex IT or cyber programs, writing acquisition strategies and managing program budgets, and you must be able to obtain an SCI clearance. Daniel's resume shows none of that experience, so skip it.
eligibility: The posting limits applicants to its listed employment authority categories, with proof. As a former contractor with no federal service, Daniel likely fits none of them.

One year of specialized experience leading complex IT or cyber programs (cost, schedule, performance, risk), developing acquisition strategies and procurement documents, managing program budgets and metrics, and coordinating with technical experts and senior leaders.
No education substitution is allowed, so Daniel must qualify on experience alone.
Must obtain and keep a Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance.
DoD Cyber Excepted Service position under 10 USC 1599f, so CES hiring rules apply.
strategy: Skip this one: it needs a year leading complex IT or cyber programs, writing acquisition strategies and managing program budgets, and his resume shows none of these.
Target better-fit roles instead, such as FEMA or Virginia VDEM program and preparedness positions, GS-9/11 management analyst jobs, or legislative and policy offices that match his strengths.
resume_bullets: Served as on-site assistant to project managers at COVID-19 mass care sites and tracked spending in pivot-table reports (2021–2022).
Found federal opportunities in SAM.gov, GovWin and the DHS acquisition forecast, and led proposal writing (2019–2024).
interview_questions: Describe a complex IT or technical program you led. How did you manage cost, schedule, performance, and risk?
How have you developed an acquisition strategy or procurement package for a technical product or service?
Tell us about a time program metrics showed a problem. What corrective action did you take?
How do you lead subject matter experts through an analysis of alternatives?
watch_outs: Specialized experience is heavily IT, cyber, and acquisition focused; emergency-management consulting alone is unlikely to qualify at GG-13.
An SCI clearance is required, and the investigation can be lengthy.
The role has no promotion potential and is on-site in Columbia, MD with only partial telework, a long commute from Manassas.
